ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: An experiment was carried out with guppies, which are brightly colored, popular aquarium fish. Three hundred guppies were added to 12 large pools. Cichlids, a voracious predator, were added to 4 of the pools. Killifish that rarely eat guppies were added to 4 other pools. No other fish were added to the last 4 pools. After 16 months, a time period that represents 10 generations for guppies, all the guppies were analyzed for size and coloration. Here are the data. According to the data, what statement is supported?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Cichlids were an agent of selection, eating the more visible, brightly colored guppies.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a line graph; the horizontal axis is time (months), and the vertical axis is the number of colored spots per fish. The three lines respectively represent "Guppies with killifish", "Guppies alone", and "Guppies with cichlids". At 0 months, all three groups start at about 12 colored spots per fish. By around 16 months, the number of colored spots in guppies together with killifish changes only slightly and remains above about 12; guppies raised alone also change only slightly and remain close to 12; but the number of colored spots in guppies together with cichlids clearly decreases, falling to below about 9 by 16 months. Reasoning: The question stem states that cichlids are voracious predators, while killifish rarely eat guppies. In the data, only the cichlids treatment group has a significant decrease in the number of colored spots, indicating that in an environment with strong predators, more conspicuous and more brightly colored guppies are more likely to be preyed upon and reduced. Therefore, cichlids exerted selection pressure on the body color of guppies and are a selection factor targeting bright colors.

method.method_draft: First describe the image data: identify the three lines and compare their changes from 0 to 16 months. Bridge these facts with natural selection: because the predator treatment specifically reduced coloration, infer that cichlids preferentially removed the more visible, brightly colored guppies.
